subject: Executive and Legislative Branch Appointment Powers
overview: The subcommittee established a work plan for Articles 2 and 3 of the City Charter, focusing on the division of power between the executive and legislative branches. Members reached a preliminary consensus on reforming appointment procedures for city boards and discussed the Council's authority to hire independent staff.

items.title: Work Plan and Organization
items.summary: The committee created a shared digital workspace and categorized charter revisions into thematic buckets including appointments, vacancies, and oversight.

items.title: Appointment and Confirmation Procedures
items.summary: Members discussed a model where mayoral appointments to boards and commissions would take effect automatically unless the Council actively rejects them within a 21-day window. The committee expressed a desire for a process that ensures transparency without creating administrative bottlenecks for volunteers.

items.title: Oversight and Information Access
items.summary: The group reviewed potential charter language to grant the Council better access to city information and explored requiring the Mayor to attend certain Council meetings.

items.title: City Council Staffing and Legal Counsel
items.summary: The committee debated the feasibility of the Council hiring its own legislative staff, noting that state law may prevent the body from maintaining independent legal counsel due to conflict of interest concerns.

items.title: Council Composition and Ward Representation
items.summary: Discussion focused on ensuring the charter can accommodate future changes in the number of wards to maintain a consistent 11-member Council body.

items.title: Future Meeting Scheduling
items.summary: The subcommittee scheduled its next meeting for November 16, 2023.
